result.markdown: --- title: "Exercise 6.1: Linear regression on puromycin data" author: "Lieven Clement, Alexandre Segers and Milan Malfait" subtitle: "statOmics, Ghent University (https://statomics.github.io)" --- # Puromycin dataset Data on the velocity of an enzymatic reaction were obtained by Treloar (1974). The number of counts per minute of radioactive product from the reaction was measured as a function of substrate concentration in parts per million (ppm) and from these counts the initial rate (or velocity) of the reaction was calculated (counts/min/min). The experiment was conducted once with the enzyme treated with Puromycin, and once with the enzyme untreated. # Goal Assess if there is an association between the substrate concentration and rate for the **treated** enzyme. Import libraries ::: {.cell} ::: # Import data In contrast to the other datasets we have worked with so far, this dataset is not available through a URL link. In stead, the data is directly available from an R package that was pre-installed in your R working environment. As such, we can simply do ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data(Puromycin) ``` ::: and an object called `Puromycin` is immediately available in your working environment. # Data wrangling For this exercise, we only want to assess if there is an association between the substrate concentration and rate for the **treated** enzyme. As such, we should filter the data so that we are left with only the treated enzymes. ::: {.cell} ::: # Data exploration Make a visualization that allows for exploring if there is a linear relationship between the substrate concentration and enzyme's rate. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} Puromycin |> ggplot(...) + # select which elements of the dataset we need to visualize ... # use a relevant plotting geometry ... # you can add some extra elements like axis labels, title, ... ``` ::: Does the relationship look linear? Can you think of any other steps that we might take to assess this relationship? ::: {.cell} ::: Now may we assume a linear relationship between the substrate concentration and the enzyme's rate? # Linear regression ## Formulate the research question ## Check the assumptions ## Interpret the model parameters of the linear model ## Interpret the results, both for the intercept as well as for the slope ## Write a conclusion that answers the research hypothesis.
